sentence: This project makes electronic materials and life-inspired materials, and studies quantum materials and the membraneless assemblies that cells form.
This project designs brain implant hardware that predicts brain activity so the implant can use less energy.
This project supports attendance at a symposium about control systems, robotics, optimization, machine learning, and autonomous systems.
This project builds machine learning methods that use isotope ratios to trace where timber products come from.
This project uses chemical and isotopic analysis to work out where archaeological materials such as ceramics and obsidian came from.
This project builds a biosensor chip that can detect single protein molecules using Raman spectroscopy.
This project studies polyploidy, which means three or more sets of chromosomes in a cell, in yeast, Arabidopsis, duckweed, Chlamydomonas, and fruit flies.
This project holds a conference on operator algebras and operator theory, with talks on topics such as free probability and noncommutative geometry.
This project tries to find out how liquid crystals can line up the chains of polymers that lack crystallinity.
This project works on growing and testing 2D materials, which are atomically thin layers, as thin films and bulk crystals.
This project builds computer methods, helped by machine learning, to model very fast processes in nanoscale materials.
This project builds a reconfigurable computing platform based on racetrack memory that can both store data and process it.
This project studies how magnetic reconnection works when strong radiative cooling is present, using theory and numerical simulations.
This project studies how the eye forms in the little skate, a cartilaginous fish that has rod photoreceptors but no cone photoreceptors.
This project builds small chips that use light to make quantum measurements in places outside the laboratory.
This project tries to find out why the fluorescence spectra of single molecules of the same dye vary and how to control that variation.
